newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat up, feed wheat down in Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat up, feed wheat down in Budapest.

text.p: Dry and warm weather prompted milling wheat and feed wheat prices to move in opposite directions on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Improved weather will speed up harvesting, thus limiting the damage to feed wheat," said Robert Vajo of brokers Termin. "But it can no longer improve the quality of milling wheat."
Milling wheat futures, the quality of which was certain to be low after more than two weeks of rainfall, have gained more than 4,000 forints per tonne since mid-July.
The rise continued on Tuesday, with all but the January and March maturities rising by the daily limit of 400 forints per tonne.
January and March rose a more modest 100 and 200 forints, having jumped sharply on Monday.
Feed wheat prices, by contrast, were mostly limit-down after three days of gains.
August fell 900 forints after three days of limit-up movement.
Maize futures finished steady to higher in minimal volumes in what was a technical correction to several days of downward movement due to good crop prospects.
Feed barley rose by between 10 and 400 forints for 1997 maturities, but turnover remained modest.
Total grains futures turnover eased to 843 lots, or 407 million forints, from Monday's 1,006 lots, or 490 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for about half the daily volume -- as it has done for most of July -- with turnover of 418 contracts.
